questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'The Four Factors of Production' refers to.
questions.a: Production needs four classic inputs - land, labour, capital and entrepreneurship - classified as factors of production; businesses combine them, paying rent for land, wages for labour and interest for capital, while profit rewards the organiser who bears the risk.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'The Four Factors of Production'.
questions.a: Land, labour, capital and enterprise join to produce; each factor earns its own return.

questions.q: Under which section is 'The Four Factors of Production' taught, and from which source text?

concepts.title: Land as a Factor: Natural Resources

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Land as a Factor: Natural Resources' refers to.
questions.a: In economics, land means far more than ground - it covers all natural gifts like soil, forests, water, air and minerals that businesses use, paying rent for them; the gifts of nature set the base on which production stands.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Land as a Factor: Natural Resources'.
questions.a: Land in economics is every free gift of nature used in production.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Land as a Factor: Natural Resources' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 7 (source: hees107.txt lines 160-175 (land encompasses natural resources, rent))

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Labour and Human Effort' refers to.
questions.a: Labour is the physical and mental human effort that turns materials into goods and services - from a farmer's fieldwork to an engineer's design - and it earns wages; the quality of labour, shaped by education and skill, decides how productive an economy can be.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Labour and Human Effort'.
questions.a: Every productive human effort, bodily or mental, is labour paid as wages.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Labour and Human Effort' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 7 (source: hees107.txt lines 175-230 (labour as a factor, wages))

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Capital and Entrepreneurship' refers to.
questions.a: Capital means the man-made aids of production - machines, tools, buildings, money invested - earning interest, while the entrepreneur supplies ideas, organises the other factors, takes risks and earns profit; technology acts as an enabler that multiplies what all four factors can produce.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Capital and Entrepreneurship'.
questions.a: Machines and money are capital; the risk-taking organiser is the entrepreneur, rewarded by profit.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Capital and Entrepreneurship' taught, and from which source text?
